messages:
maya: quick sync: we need a compact, privacy-preserving identifier for public telemetry that still supports cost attribution and basic grouping.

ryan: options: keyed HMAC per-tenant (deterministic) vs reversible KV mapping. HMAC safer, KV gives debugability.

elena: constraints from privacy/legal: no raw trace ids in exported buckets. reversible mapping only under opt-in with audit trail.

kevin: infra: HMAC(tenant_salt, trace_id) -> 16 bytes binary token stored as `trace_export_token`. Binary index keeps size small. Reversible cache adds write QPS and storage; gate behind enterprise feature flag.

maya: rollout plan: 1) emit `trace_export_token` alongside raw in staging; 2) default HMAC-only for public sinks; 3) pilot mapping cache for 3 enterprise tenants behind FF.

ryan: open questions: token length (128-bit recommended), retention defaults for mapping cache (7d default, up to 90d opt-in), and cataloging saved queries that rely on raw prefix searches.

elena: security checklist: KMS-wrapped keys per-region, strict IAM on mapping reads, mandatory audit logs, and 2-person approval for raw retrievals.

kevin: action items: bench binary vs hex index size (ryan), estimate mapping cache cost for pilot (kevin), draft console copy & opt-in flow (maya). I'll kick a PoC deploy.

ingest-bot: deploy queued: feature/trace-export-poc -> staging :rocket:

maya: will write RFC with migration/backfill steps and compatibility notes. cc security/legal.
